objective: Make long-horizon pause, revise, retract, resume, and rollback requests monotonic, intent-generation-bound, checkpoint-aware, and safe around irreversible side effects.

research_inputs.finding: Interruptible long-horizon agents must handle addition, revision, and retraction of user intent during execution with persistent environment state; multiple sequential interruptions require explicit adaptation and recovery semantics.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds monotonic pause, revise, retract, and resume transitions bound to task intent and generation, while emitting control receipts rather than executing process control.

research_inputs.finding: Checkpoint restore cannot undo external side effects; LLM agents can regenerate different requests after restore, so retry-safe identifiers alone do not prevent duplicate or replayed irreversible actions. Safe recovery requires replay-or-fork semantics and recording irreversible effects.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds checkpoint trace and side-effect watermarks and returns require_fork when rollback crosses an irreversible-effect boundary; it never claims that external effects were undone.

features: pause, revise, retract, resume, and rollback operation admission
task, intent digest, generation, freshness, trace sequence, checkpoint, and side-effect watermark binding
monotonic transition sequence and replay fence
require_fork verdict when rollback crosses irreversible-effect watermark
receipt-only control result with process_paused=false, rollback_executed=false, and external_effects_undone=false

benchmark.scope: local Python control-plane admission overhead; excludes process control, credential revocation, external rollback, network, storage, tools, and production approval latency

limitations: The contract validates caller-supplied checkpoint and side-effect watermarks; it does not independently observe external services or undo external effects.
The contract emits a pause, revision, resume, or fork-required verdict but does not pause processes, revoke credentials, execute rollback, or create a new branch.
The benchmark does not establish interruption adaptation quality, duplicate-side-effect reduction, recovery time, tool success, AGI capability, production efficacy, or Linux superiority.
No physical hardware, external reviewer, independent builder, live multihost environment, or production approval was exercised.
